issues.description: The solution declares Genre.name as a private property, but the Client implementation (and the problem description) expects to access genre.name. In Swift, `private` restricts access to the declaring file, so accessing `genre.name` from Client.swift (a different file) will cause a compilation error and contradicts the problem requirement that Genre has a name accessible for output.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the Genre.name property non-private so it can be accessed from other files in the module. For example, remove the `private` modifier (use `let name: String`) or explicitly mark it `public` if broader visibility is desired. This preserves the intended API where Client can read the genre's name for printing.
